messages.subject: flatpak
messages.body_plain:
hi rachel,

Am Sonntag, 22. September 2024, 04:55:57 CEST schrieb Rachel Schrader:
> I was curious if I could still get rkward on flatpak. The homepage as a
> link for it but it appears to be broken and I don't see it on flathub.

currently, we are officially providing AppImage builds of the latest version 
of RKWard:

  https://rkward.kde.org/Binaries_and_Build_Scripts.html

> I am using debian I don't think rkward is in the stable repos.

the reason for this confusing state is the current lack of support for plasma 
6 in some distributions, while the development of RKWard has moved to that up-
to-date branch of KDE and we don't have the resources to support both, plasma 
5 and 6.

so for the time being, the AppImage is what we recommend to use. hopefully 
this is a transitional phase until automatic packaging for these distros 
becomes available again. but given that kubuntu LTS was just released with 
plasma 5, it looks like the AppImage builds are likely to stay with us for a 
couple of years.


viele grüße :: m.eik

-- 
  dipl. psych. meik michalke
  institut f"ur experimentelle psychologie
  abt. f"ur diagnostik und differentielle psychologie

messages.body_plain:
Adding to Meik's reply:

On Sat, 21 Sep 2024 20:55:57 -0600
Rachel Schrader <rachels at mailbox.org> wrote:
> I was curious if I could still get rkward on flatpak. The homepage as
> a link for it but it appears to be broken and I don't see it on
> flathub.

I don't seem to find that link. Could you point me to it so I can
remove / replace it?

For some context on why we are not providing flatpak: We've
experimented with that, but the flatpak sandboxing is simply too
restrictive. I order to be able to install R add-on packages, we'd need
to be able to interface with a system-installed R, but that seems to be
out of reach.

As Meik already wrote, we do provide official AppImages, however, which
do no suffer from the same limitation.

Regards
Thomas
